$comment: The app's key screens, captured from each platform's preview build (#331). Each screen opens by deep link (sdachurchapp://<path>) after its settings are saved; each variant adds the settings listed under variants. Screenshots are named <platform>/<screen>-<variant>.png. checks lists automatic image checks for a screen, mustShowLines regular expressions that some line of its text must match (or { line, minLeft } for a line that must also start at least minLeft of the way across, such as right-aligned text), mustNotShowLines ones that no line may match, variantRules more of either for one variant, and tabs false for a screen without the tab bar, such as the Bible while reading (scripts/check-screens.cjs); appStore lists, per App Store language, the shots to upload, in order. Leave out screens that show members' names or photos, such as the bulletin, the team page, the fellowship page, and the worship schedule. See docs/operations/native-builds.md.

screens.name: home
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text: the app at 200% with the iPhone's accessibility-large text (2×), held to 3.2× by the combined cap, as with Android's largest font at 200%, where the tab labels used to wrap (#380). Their verse-card buttons and heading must show whole words, not “Shar” or “Versícul / o” (#385). Vision reads each button's icon as a character (“‹ Share Verse”), so the button rules match anywhere in the line; the verse changes daily, and a long one, such as John 1:1 in English or most verses in Spanish, pushes the lower button, or both, below the shot, so English checks only “Share Verse” and Spanish only its heading. The tab-label check fails on a wrapped label, or one pushed up out of the tab bar's area by an overgrown bar. Not the iPhone's very largest size: at about 6× in all, page titles break mid-word, which isn't a useful baseline.

screens.name: bible-dual
screens.$comment: The header's translation button in full: the 文A icon (read as XA), the EN badge, and both names, not cut to B… or C… (#376).

screens.name: bible-dual-back
screens.$comment: Opened from Home, so the header also has a back arrow and less room. When it's tight, the translation button gives up its 文A icon first, then the length of its names, then its badges (#376). At 150% and 200% only the icon goes: the EN badge and both full names stay.

screens.name: bible-cuv
screens.$comment: Mandarin is the default narrator, so the audio button shows 國語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-cantonese
screens.$comment: With the Cantonese narrator chosen, the audio button shows 粵語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-after-spanish
screens.$comment: The Spanish Bible was open with the CUV underneath, then a link opens the CUV. Its book names must replace the Spanish ones, which once stayed until a restart (#373). The interface is English, as when the bug showed, so Vision reads the dock in English first and misses 詩篇; it reads a stale Salmos reliably.

screens.name: bible-cuvs
screens.$comment: Simplified characters, so the audio button shows 国语.

screens.name: bible-scrolled
screens.$comment: Opens at John 3:14, so earlier verses sit under the status bar; checks it stays clear.

screens.name: bible-long-chapter
screens.$comment: Psalm 119 from verse 100, for three-digit verse numbers at large text sizes.

screens.name: bible-higgaion-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:16 in the BSB ends with "Higgaion Selah", plain text after the verse's poetry lines in the HelloAO data. At the default text size the reader shows it right-aligned under the verse, so it must start in the right half of the screen.

screens.name: bible-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:20 in the BSB ends with "Selah" alone, right-aligned on its own line, so it must start in the right half of the screen. The rule needs a line starting with Selah, so 9:16's "Higgaion Selah" can't satisfy it.

screens.name: explore
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text check the tab labels at about 4× text, as on Home (#380). max is the app at 200% with the iPhone's very largest text, about 6× before the combined cap (MAX_COMBINED_TEXT_SCALE) held it to 3.2×; at 6× the Library card's title read "Libr".

screens.name: library-children
screens.$comment: Books by other writers lead the Children shelf, and Ellen G. White's books for adults stay on her own shelf (#391).

screens.name: library-youth
screens.$comment: Pastor Hsi leads the Youth shelf, ahead of Ellen G. White's books, and The Pilgrim's Progress follows in each reader's language: its 1869 Mandarin edition for Chinese readers, and Chapel Library's for Spanish (#391). Its English and Spanish titles wrap, so only their first lines are checked.

screens.name: sabbath-school
screens.$comment: The first children's age group shows every week, in each language (#338).

screens.name: hymnal-selection
screens.$comment: The hymnal page (#413): a carousel of the hymnals, the app language's first, then the 1985 ↔ 505 lookup chip, the picked hymnal's search, and its hymns, each 1985 or 505 hymn with the other hymnal's number. Vision reads the 文A icon in a chip as XA and a row's treble clef as a character, so those lines are matched anywhere.

screens.name: hymnal
screens.$comment: A link to one hymn, as from the bulletin: the hymnal page opens on the SDA Hymnal with just that hymn, marked, its 505 number, and Show all hymns, which at 150% may fall below the shot.

screens.name: hymnal-chinese
screens.$comment: An older hymnal route opens the hymnal page with that hymnal picked: the 506, not the 505 a Chinese interface would show first. Its cover photo is cropped to the carousel's 2:3 frame.

screens.name: give
screens.$comment: Zelle stays hidden until its address is ready (#392). When shown, its heading sits just above the tab bar.
